# edgeos_wireguard_interface (Resource)

A WireGuard interface (`interfaces wireguard <name>`). Needs the WireGuard package for EdgeOS on the router.

Peers are managed with `edgeos_wireguard_peer`; this resource never touches them on update. Destroying the interface deletes the whole node, including every peer, managed by Terraform or not.

Prefer a key file for `private_key` (`/config/auth/wg0.key`, created with `wg genkey` on the router), so the private key never ends up in the Terraform state. An inline key works too but is stored in the state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Create the key on the router first, so it never leaves the device:
#   umask 077 && wg genkey > /config/auth/wg0.key
resource "edgeos_wireguard_interface" "wg0" {
  name        = "wg0"
  description = "Road warriors"
  addresses   = ["10.8.0.1/24"]
  listen_port = 51820
  mtu         = 1420
  private_key = "/config/auth/wg0.key"
  firewall_in = edgeos_firewall_name.wg_in.name
}

resource "edgeos_firewall_name" "wg_in" {
  name           = "WG_IN"
  default_action = "accept"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Interface name from `wg0` to `wg999`. Changing it creates a new interface.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) Private key of the interface: either the base64 key itself or an absolute path to a file on the router that holds it, such as `/config/auth/wg0.key`. Files outside `/config` are lost on a firmware upgrade. If the router hides the value from the API session, the configured value is kept in state, so a key changed on the router behind Terraform's back is then not detected.

### Optional

- `addresses` (Set of String) Addresses of the interface with prefix length, such as `10.8.0.1/24` or `fd00:8::1/64`.
- `description` (String) Free text description.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Keep the interface in the config but switch it off (the `disable` node). Defaults to `false`.
- `firewall_in` (String) IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic coming in from the tunnel (`firewall in name`), usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`.
- `firewall_local` (String) IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic from the tunnel to the router itself (`firewall local name`), usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`.
- `firewall_out` (String) IPv4 firewall rule set applied to traffic going out to the tunnel (`firewall out name`), usually `edgeos_firewall_name.x.name`.
- `fwmark` (Number) Firewall mark set on the interface's outgoing packets, for policy routing.
- `listen_port` (Number) UDP port to listen on. Unset picks a random port, which only suits interfaces that never accept incoming handshakes.
- `mtu` (Number) MTU from 68 to 9000. WireGuard uses 1420 when unset.
- `route_allowed_ips` (Boolean) Add routes for the peers' `allowed_ips` through this interface. Unset leaves the EdgeOS default (`true`).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The interface name.
- `public_key` (String) Public key derived from an inline `private_key`, for the peers' configs. Null when `private_key` is a file path; run `wg pubkey < /config/auth/wg0.key` on the router instead.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_wireguard_interface.wg0
  id = "wg0"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <interface name>
terraform import edgeos_wireguard_interface.wg0 wg0
```
